title: Least-Privilege Gap Triage and Evidence Automation Plan - Q3 2025
body:
Purpose:
Capture a pragmatic triage and automation plan for the Q3 quarterly least-privilege recertification focusing on RBAC v2 role cleanup, audit evidence automation, and SIEM export mappings. This is a working doc — decisions, open questions, and next actions are below.

Scope:
- All privileged roles across Hosted API, Dedicated control plane, and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)
- Evidence types: role assignment snapshots, approval records, justification notes, MFA status, and ticket links
- SIEM exports to the centralized Splunk index and the new audit-log-schema.v2 ingestion pipeline

Background / why now:
RBAC v2 rollout introduced several composite roles and temporary elevation flows. During the last manual recert we saw three recurring problems: stale service-account assignments, ad-hoc temporary privileged requests with no ticket linkage, and inconsistent evidence formats that block automated ingestion into SIEM and the compliance dashboard. Q3 initiative: reduce manual triage by automating evidence capture for 75% of flagged assignments and stabilize SIEM parsing rules for RBAC v2 events.

High-level goals (Q3):
- Define a stable audit-log schema for privilege-grant/revoke/elevation that supports automated evidence linking.
- Implement ETL/mapping for SIEM exports so recertification queries return structured columns: role_id, principal_type, principal_id, grant_time, grant_via, approver_id, justification_id, evidence_url.
- Run two pilot recert cycles with automation enabled (pilot teams: eng-serving-runtime, product-dedicated).
- Reduce manual review workload by >= 50% vs. Q2.

Triage matrix (how we decide action for each flagged item):
- Category A: Service accounts with no recent owner (age > 90d) -> auto-flag + create ticket to platform-eng; mark 'suspend after 14d' if no owner assigned.
- Category B: Humans with privileged roles but no approval ticket -> send automated notification to manager + require ticket upload within 7d; if not provided, move to temporary suspension.
- Category C: Temporary elevation not recorded in RBAC audit log -> task to SRE to backfill events using session logs (if available) or mark for manual attestation.
- Category D: Legacy composite roles that map 1:many to v2 roles -> schedule role decomposition and owner reassignment (owner must accept in 21d).

Evidence automation checklist (for each recert item):
1) Snapshot capture: generate role assignment CSV snapshot (one per principal) via /admin/export-roles API at recert start.
2) Approval linkage: extract approval artifacts from Jira/GHR via webhook or tag parsing. Acceptable artifacts: Jira ticket id with approver and timestamps, signed approval emails (in PDF), or console-logged AR workflows.
3) MFA attestation: query identity provider to include mfa_enrolled boolean.
4) Justification policy: capture free-text justification and attach as "justification_id" stored in evidence S3 bucket (immutable, retention 7y for privileged).
5) Evidence manifest: produce JSONL manifest (one line per assignment) with canonical fields for SIEM ingestion.

Note on formats:
- Canonical fields (required): role_id, role_name, principal_id, principal_type (user|service|group), granted_by, grant_time (ISO8601), grant_source (console|api|ticket), approver_id, justification_id, evidence_url, ttl_until (if temporary).
- Accept plain CSV/JSONL outputs from the admin export. The SIEM ETL will normalize.

SIEM export / parsing rules (Splunk pipeline draft):
- New event type: rbac.change.v2 with sub-events: grant, revoke, elevate, approve, backfill.
- Use explicit field extraction: role_id, principal_id, grant_time, grant_source, justification_id. Avoid relying on free-text messages.
- Example SPL query for recert: index=rbac_logs sourcetype=rbac.change.v2 grant_time>="2025-09-01" | stats latest(approver_id) as approver by role_id principal_id
- Backfill strategy: if rbac.change.v2 missing approver_id, attempt to enrich from sitemap of Jira links via join on justification_id. If no match, mark manual.

Role-owner mapping (initial assignments):
- rn_role_admins -> owner: Marco Liu (platform-engineering)
- runtime_ops_write -> owner: Samira Patel (serving-runtime SRE lead)
- billing_admin -> owner: Aisha Bell (finance-and-legal liasion)
- private_deploy_ops -> owner: Jon Reyes (private-deployments)
Action: owners must confirm or nominate an alternate by 2025-10-10.

Pilot plan and timeline:
- Week 0 (kickoff): agree on canonical fields and SIEM SPL queries (security + infra).
- Week 1-2: implement export hooks and evidence manifest generation in admin/export-roles (eng infra).
- Week 3: SIEM ETL team (observability) add parsing rules and map fields.
- Week 4: Run dry-run recert on pilot teams -> produce automated report and manual review queues.
- Week 5-6: Iterate on mapping, fix false positives, add enrichment for Jira link parsing.
- Week 7: Full pilot recert run and retrospective.

Manual reviewer UX notes (for console and spreadsheet output):
- Show "evidence_url" as single-click to immutable artifact.
- Provide quick actions: Confirm, Escalate (creates ticket), Request more evidence (sends templated email).
- Prioritize items where principle_type=user && mfa_enrolled=false; these require human confirmation.

Metrics to track (success criteria):
- % of flagged items with automated evidence >= 75%
- Mean time to remediation for Category A/B items < 21 days
- Number of manual escalations per recert cycle <= 20% of total flagged

Open questions / risks:
- How do we guarantee evidence immutability for externally linked approvals (e.g., SaaS ticketing)? Current plan: snapshot to S3 at time of recert and store hash in manifest. Need legal sign-off for retention policy.
- Will RBAC v2 composite roles require per-tenant decomposition to properly map owners? Risk: one-size decomposition may break delegated admin flows.
- SIEM ingestion limits: Splunk ingestion costs could spike with verbose manifest — need compressed daily bundles and dedup logic.

Next actions (owners assigned):
- Marco: finalize canonical field list and update admin/export-roles API (due 2025-09-25).
- Samira: prototype manifest generator and run dry export for serving-runtime (due 2025-10-02).
- Aisha: coordinate Jira webhook schema and test approval extraction (due 2025-09-29).
- Jon: validate private deployment evidence paths and sample artifact uploads (due 2025-09-30).
- Priya (owner): schedule pilot kickoff and send invites (done).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally captures early operational decisions rather than final policy language. Expect changes after pilot.
- If you are an owner assigned above, reply in-thread with acceptance or an alternate.

Appendix: quick example manifest line (CSV):
role_id,role_name,principal_id,principal_type,granted_by,grant_time,grant_source,approver_id,justification_id,evidence_url,ttl_until
rn_role_admins,Platform Admins,svc-kafka-prod,service,iaas-bot,2025-08-18T11:22:00Z,api,con-3344,just-887,https://s3.redwood.ai/evidence/just-887.pdf,2026-08-18T11:22:00Z

Related tickets / references (please add more if you find them):
- SEC-PI-578: RBAC v2 evidence pipeline (owner: Priya)
- INFRA-2041: admin/export-roles enhancements (owner: Marco)
- OBS-910: Splunk parsing rules for rbac.change.v2 (owner: Elena, observability)

End of document.
